Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires are on the field and the Bangladesh fielders are well spread out in the field. Syed Aziz and Zubaidi Zulkifle will open the innings for Malaysia. Ripon Mondol has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the first half of the match comes to an end with Bangladesh putting a 116 on the board. We saw the Malaysian bowlers start off incredibly well but the batters made a good comeback towards the end of the innings. The Malaysian batters will have to bat watchfully looking at the pitch and the good amount of turn the spinners are getting. Will Bangladesh live up to their expectations or will Malaysia cause a massive upset? We will get to know in a while. Grab a cup of coffee and join us again in some time for the run chase.

Malaysia had a dream start to this quarter-finals taking three wickets in quick succession. They however failed to keep the pressure on and allowed the batters to play freely. Some sloppy fielding and missed chances made sure that the runs kept coming for the opposition. Vijay Unni looked in good rhythm initially but leaked a lot of runs in the later stages of the match. Pavandeep Singh bowled a brilliant spell and took 2 wickets with Anwar Rahman taking one. Overall, a good bowling effort made sure that the target was not on the higher side and was still chaseable with the form of the Malaysian batters. The batters will have to bat with some responsibility on this tricky pitch and preserve wickets.

Bangladesh was put on the back foot pretty early on in the innings after losing 3 wickets for just 3 runs. Saif Hassan and Afif Hossain decided to take on the bowlers and started playing aggressively. Afif Hossain was dismissed after playing some amazing shots but he set the tone for the coming batters. Shahadat Hossain also played a fine steady inning with Jaker Ali providing a good end. The star batter was the skipper Saif Hassan who completed a fine half-century playing a captain's knock. It is now to the bowlers to defend a 117.

What a comeback from Bangladesh here in the first innings. A very entertaining first half of the match comes to an end. Malaysia seemed to come out on top initially but the Bangladeshi batters made sure that they stayed in the game. They fought hard on a tricky pitch and put 116 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! The Malaysian players spread out to take their respective field positions. Parvez Hossain Emon and Mahmudul Hasan Joy are the two openers for Bangladesh. We will see spin straightaway as Pavandeep Singh has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that, both sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Malaysia's first followed by the national anthem of Bangladesh.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Jaker Ali (WK), Parvez Hossain Emon, Zakir Hasan, Rakibul Hasan, Saif Hassan (C), Rishad Hossain, Shahadat Hossain, Mahmudul Hasan Joy, Sumon Khan, Ripon Mondol, Afif Hossain.

Malaysia (Playing XI) - Ahmad Faiz (C), Zubaidi Zulkifle, Ainool Hafizs (WK), Muhammad Amir Azim, Anwar Rahman, Pavandeep Singh, Sharvin Muniandy, Syazrul Idrus, Syed Aziz, Vijay Unni, Virandeep Singh.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of Bangladesh. They have elected to BAT first.

Malaysia has put up an amazing performance so far in this tournament. They have been bowling and batting well putting up impressive targets. Syed Aziz is the centurion in this competition and his form will be a great help to his team in this match. Their bowling unit is strong too with everyone bowling upto the mark and there are no weak links. This will be a thrilling encounter as both teams will fight for the one spot in the semis. Stay with us the live action will take center stage shortly. Toss and team news will be coming up soon.

Bangladesh have to play their second-string squad with the main one being in India for the World Cup. They however have some experience on their side with Afif Hossain, Mahmudul Hasan Joy, and Yasir Ali being the senior players. Saif Hassan is also in a good touch and will hope to provide a solid opening to the innings. The only issue is their bowling department which lacks the experience at this level. However, they will fight strong and are the favorites in this encounter.
... MATCH DAY ...

The 4th and final quarter-final clash in the Men's Cricket Competition at the Asian Games sees a clash between 2010 Gold medal winners Bangladesh and Malaysia at the ZJUT Cricket ground in Hangzhou. This is a big clash given what's at stake and with Bangladesh having to field a second-string side due to the upcoming Cricket World Cup, Malaysia might just fancy their chances. Bangladesh do however have a few players who have played at the highest level with the likes of Afif Hossain, Mahmudul Hasan Joy, and Yasir Ali on the side. They will be led by opening batter Saif Hassan who has had some fantastic performances at the domestic level and for the Bangladesh A side as well over the years. The batting does have experience and the middle order seems well-balanced but the bowling is a bit inexperienced. Malaysia on the other hand have reached this stage on the back of a couple of thumping victories over Singapore and Thailand and in both of those matches, they kept the opposition to under 90 runs, also having scored a mammoth 264 against the latter. Syed Aziz scored an incredible 126 against Thailand and the batting in general has been fantastic. The same goes for the bowling as the attack has performed as a unit rather than relying on one or two particular bowlers. Malaysia will be aware of the fact that this is a completely different ball game but will surely be pumped up and ready for it. Who are you backing to get the win?
